evidence.AC1: POST /todos with {"title":"past","dueDate":"2026-10-13"} returned 201 with dueDate "2026-10-13" (date only, no time). POST without dueDate returned 201 with dueDate null.
evidence.AC2: PATCH /todos/2 {"dueDate":"2026-09-01"} returned 200 and the dueDate changed from 2026-10-15 to 2026-09-01. PATCH /todos/3 {"dueDate":null} returned 200 and dueDate became null. A PATCH that only changed the title left a null dueDate null.
evidence.AC3: POST with dueDate "2026-02-30", "14/10/2026" and "2026-10-14T10:00:00" each returned 400 with {"error":"dueDate must be a date in the form YYYY-MM-DD"}. PATCH with "2026-02-30" also returned 400.
evidence.AC4: Today is 2026-10-14 (UTC). GET /todos?overdue=true returned only the todos due 2026-10-13 and 2026-09-01. Not returned: the todo due today (2026-10-14), the todo with no due date, and the todo with a past due date that I marked done (it shows overdue:false). Today-due and future-due todos show overdue:false.
evidence.AC5: The browser snapshot of / shows each dated todo with its due date next to the title (e.g. 'past 2026-10-13 überfällig', 'donepast ✓ 2026-10-01'). Todos without a due date show none.
evidence.AC6: In the page snapshot, 'überfällig' appears only on the two overdue todos (due 2026-10-13 and 2026-09-01). It does not appear on the todo with no due date, the todo with no due date after its date was removed, or the done todo with a past due date.
evidence.AC7: The page has a checkbox labelled 'nur überfällige'. Clicking it reduced the list to the two overdue todos (past and future, the latter now due 2026-09-01); the other three todos disappeared.
